question: What services does BPI offer?
html:
BPI is a communications and public-affairs company. Today the work covers political and advocacy campaigns, reputation work and public affairs for regulated sectors, delivered from 14 offices in 6 countries (BPI public filings). The growth plan adds packaged retainers and named sector practices on top of that core (BPI growth plan).

What we do today

  • Political and advocacy campaigns. Federal committees paid BPI $115.3M in the 2024 cycle (BPI public filings). That figure is gross billings, mostly pass-through media spend, not BPI revenue.
  • Reputation work. Reputation work for the AI era is a core part of the thesis (BPI growth plan).
  • Public affairs for regulated sectors. Energy, AI and health are the named focus areas (BPI growth plan).
  • Transatlantic coverage. London is the #2 hub and Germany the #3 market, built through European add-ons (BPI growth plan).

The context does not include a formal service catalogue or a revenue split by service line. BPI's own service-line revenue and client mix would show how large each line is.

What the growth plan adds

PhaseOfferStatus
OneSignalOS retainers: narrative monitoring, synthetic message testing, outcome dashboardsPlanned; launch targeted by Oct 2027 (est.)
TwoNamed practices: AI and tech policy, energy and critical minerals, health (Boston), litigation and oversightPlanned
TwoFederal capture team for about $250M of tracked agency communications recompetesPlanned; no prime awards today

(BPI growth plan)

  • SignalOS would be sold first through the 2026 Reputation Resilience Index briefings. In that research, 81% of adults say AI makes false rumors too easy to spread (BPI growth plan).
  • Add-ons are meant to be specialist shops. AI agents would handle monitoring, compliant drafting and audience testing (BPI growth plan).

Why the mix is shifting

  • Federal political billings went from $3.1M in 2022 to $115.3M in 2024 (BPI growth plan).
  • The roadmap targets about 55% recurring revenue by Oct 2029 (est.) (BPI growth plan).

Moving the service mix from election-cycle projects to always-on retainers is the main lever on the value gap, because buyers pay more for predictable revenue than for a strong election year.

Next actions

  1. Build a service-line revenue and margin split for FY2025, separating fee revenue from pass-through media.
  2. Map each of the six add-ons to the service lines and practices above. The context does not describe their capabilities.
  3. Set a SignalOS pilot list drawn from Reputation Resilience Index briefing attendees, with target retainer counts.
  4. Confirm which planned practices already have named leads and active clients.
